ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a curve graph of vapor pressure changing with temperature, with the horizontal axis as Temperature (°C) and the vertical axis as Vapor pressure (torr). The figure has curves for liquids such as Diethyl ether, Ethyl alcohol (ethanol), Water, and Ethylene glycol, and has a horizontal line at about 760 torr labeled Normal boiling point; near the normal boiling point of the ethanol curve it is labeled 78.3°C. Reasoning: The external pressure given in the problem is 0.0724 atm. Convert it to the vertical-axis unit in the figure: 0.0724 × 760 torr = 55.024 torr, approximately 55 torr. When a liquid boils, its vapor pressure equals the external pressure, so on the graph take about 55 torr, move horizontally to the Ethyl alcohol (ethanol) curve, then read downward to the horizontal-axis temperature, approximately 20°C.
